title: Pre-Analysis — Leading Edge Panel Fastener Standard Against the Repair Population

ata.title: Wing Leading Edge — Fixed Leading Edge Structure

abstract: Closed work order establishing what happens to aircraft that already carry land repairs when the reduced fastener pitch is embodied, and confirming that the two can coexist.

sections.objective: Establish what the reduced fastener pitch and bonded anchor nut strip standard means for aircraft that already carry elongated hole repairs in the panel land, which on the high-utilisation fleet is most of them. The commercial case assumed the repairs would simply be superseded and that assumption had not been tested.
sections.findings_summary: The assumption is broadly right but not universally. Where a land carries oversize anchor nuts or bushed inserts, the new sixty millimetre pitch drills between them and the repairs become irrelevant, which is what the case assumed. Where a land carries the local doubler repair the new pitch cannot be drilled without going through it, and those lands need the doubler removing first or the panel replacing. The repair scheme records the doubler route on the panel map, so the population is knowable in advance rather than discovered at the visit, which turns a surprise into a planning item. The flood test in the installation task is the other useful finding: it is the only step that proves the seal has seated, and on a repaired land the seal groove may be locally distorted in a way that only the flood test would catch.
sections.next_steps: Publish the interaction so that operators can extract the affected lands from their panel maps before the visit is planned. Keep the flood test mandatory on every panel including repaired ones. No change to the modification.

tasks.title: Extract the land repair population from the fleet panel maps
Establish which repair routes obstruct the new pitch
Confirm the flood test applies to repaired lands

evidence.similarity_note: Both entity linking on the panel and cleat part numbers and similarity on the land repair vocabulary returned this scheme.

expected_findings.rationale: The local land doubler route occupies the material the new sixty millimetre pitch would drill into. A land carrying that repair cannot take the new pitch without the doubler being removed or the panel replaced, and the modification says nothing about it.
expected_findings.resolution: Publish the interaction and instruct operators to extract affected lands from the panel map before planning the visit.

evidence.similarity_note: Found by entity linking on the panel and bracket part numbers the task calls out.

expected_findings.rationale: The flood test is the only step that proves the seal has seated. On a repaired land the seal groove may be locally distorted and the test is the only thing that would find it, so it must not be treated as optional on repaired panels.
expected_findings.resolution: State explicitly that the flood test applies to repaired lands without exception.

evidence.similarity_note: Reached from the modification to its retrofit bulletin.

expected_findings.rationale: The bulletin instructs that both wings are brought to the same standard in one visit, which is right, but says nothing about what to do when one land on one wing carries a doubler repair.
expected_findings.resolution: Add the repaired land case to the bulletin planning information.

type_data.conclusion: Closed. The two coexist except on doubler-repaired lands, which are knowable in advance.
